justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mild upward drift from what I'd assume was a recent price around $413–414 for the underlying asset (likely SPY or a similar broad equity index given the price range). At the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the prevailing price with only a small expected move, reflecting the tendency of equity markets to exhibit near-random walk behavior over very short horizons with a slight positive drift built in from the long-run equity risk premium. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to $416, again incorporating that modest positive drift while acknowledging that a week gives more time for mean-reverting or trending forces to play out. At the one-month horizon, $418 reflects roughly one month of expected drift, consistent with annualized returns in the mid-to-high single digits applied to this price level.

The confidence interval widths were primarily driven by realized and implied volatility assumptions. For a one-day window, typical daily volatility for a broad equity index runs around 1–1.5%, which translates to a range of roughly plus or minus $6–8 around the point estimate, consistent with my $401–$428 band. At the one-week horizon, volatility scales with the square root of time, widening the interval to roughly plus or minus $24, and at one month it widens further to approximately plus or minus $46. These widths also incorporate some additional uncertainty about the volatility regime itself — whether we're in a calm or turbulent market environment — which adds a layer of uncertainty beyond simple historical volatility scaling.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes well outside my stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data (e.g., a surprising inflation print, disappointing employment figures, or renewed banking sector stress) could trigger sharp selling, easily breaching the lower bounds especially at the one-week and one-month horizons. Geopolitical shocks or unexpected central bank communications could similarly produce outsized moves. On the upside, a strong earnings season, a dovish pivot surprise from the Federal Reserve, or a resolution of an ongoing macro uncertainty could drive prices above the upper bounds. Fat-tailed events — the kind that standard volatility models systematically underestimate — represent the chief reason why realized outcomes occasionally land far outside even 90% confidence intervals, and that caveat applies fully here.
